cards.title: Recognize when SEO has shifted to old-style purchase pages
cards.summary: Google AI mode increasingly cites homepages, category and product pages over listicles, changing what to optimize.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to keep investing in listicle/blog content versus product, category and homepage pages for AI visibility.

cards.title: Do GEO research before touching pages
cards.summary: Find where AI sources its answers for your target prompts, then reverse-engineer your way into those sources.
cards.use_when: Starting an AI-visibility campaign for a store and deciding which channels and pages to prioritize.

cards.title: Spend 70-80% of GEO effort on good SEO first
cards.summary: Fix technical SEO and build product/service/location pages before chasing off-site AI tactics.
cards.use_when: Allocating budget and team effort across a store's AI-visibility program.

cards.title: Screen growth tactics by your time horizon
cards.summary: Ask what a tactic does to your brand in two or three years before scaling it, especially if you plan to be around long term.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to adopt a fast but risky AI-spam content or link tactic for a store with long-term customers.

cards.title: Capture brand impressions from AI answers
cards.summary: Treat logo or link placement beneath AI overviews as paid-ad-equivalent brand exposure, not just lost clicks.
cards.use_when: Evaluating the value of AI overview presence when organic click-through has fallen for a store's queries.

cards.title: Query fan-out: why AI citation needs topical coverage, not one keyword
cards.summary: AI assistants expand a single prompt into many synthetic sub-queries, so you must be relevant across a whole topic rather than one head keyword.
cards.use_when: Planning product-category content or PDP/editorial coverage and deciding which topics to own so your products can be surfaced inside AI answers.

cards.title: Brand gap analysis to find missed AI citations
cards.summary: Run a brand gap analysis to surface where your brand is mentioned-but-not-cited, where competitors win, and which topics AI associates with others.
cards.use_when: Auditing AI visibility before choosing which ecommerce content, PDP or mention-building work to do next.

cards.title: The AI Filter: deciding when a keyword is a trap vs an unlinked-mention play
cards.summary: Test each target keyword by asking whether an AI overview fully answers it; informational queries that AI 'eats' should be targeted for unlinked brand mentions, not clicks.
cards.use_when: Doing keyword research for a store and deciding where to chase clicks versus where to aim for brand mention inside AI answers.

cards.title: BLUF writing for AI and human parsing
cards.summary: Bottom Line Up Front: start every section with the answer, because both people and LLMs weight the beginning and end of a passage more heavily than the middle.
cards.use_when: Writing or rewriting PDP copy, category intros, buying guides or FAQ blocks so AI can extract your answer cleanly.

cards.title: Atomic content and entity-rich writing for chunk extraction
cards.summary: Make each section understandable out of context and pack it with specific entities and relationships so AI can extract and connect meaning.
cards.use_when: Structuring PDP sections, feature blocks, comparison pages or guides that AI may pull as isolated fragments.

cards.title: Content format and freshness to get cited (length doesn't matter)
cards.summary: AI citations favor lists/comparisons and freshly updated pages, not word count; over half of cited pages are under 1,000 words.
cards.use_when: Deciding the format and update cadence for store buying guides, comparison pages and category content.

cards.title: Earn brand mentions in three tiers of pages
cards.summary: Branded web mentions had the strongest correlation with AI overview visibility in a study of 75,000 brands — stronger than backlinks or domain rating — so get named on other people's pages.
cards.use_when: Planning off-site AEO work (PR, lists, community, creator) to increase how often AI recommends your store.

cards.title: YouTube AEO: target search hits over viral hits
cards.summary: YouTube is the most cited domain in Google AI overviews and YouTube mentions showed the strongest correlation with ChatGPT visibility in the source's data — build evergreen search-hit videos, not viral spikes.
cards.use_when: Planning video content or creator sponsorships to increase AI visibility for your store.

cards.title: Technical AEO: don't accidentally block AI crawlers
cards.summary: Check robots.txt for disallow rules against GPTBot, OAI Search Bot, ClaudeBot and Google Extended, since Cloudflare's AI-bot setting defaults to blocking GPTBot.
cards.use_when: First-step technical audit before any AEO content or mention work on your store's domain.

cards.title: Measuring AEO: AI referral traffic, bot activity and self-reported attribution
cards.summary: Track AI referral traffic (as a directional undercount), AI citation-bot activity on your pages, and 'How did you hear about us?' survey attribution to capture otherwise-hidden AI impact.
cards.use_when: Setting up store analytics for AI-driven discovery and deciding which channels actually drive sign-ups or purchases.

cards.title: Building a custom AEO strategy by matching gap to priority
cards.summary: Sequence AEO work: technical check first, measurement setup, then fix the biggest brand-gap by matching gap type to the right intervention.
cards.use_when: Turning AI-visibility findings into a prioritized action plan for your store.

cards.title: Set up a persistent AI project for SEO and product research
cards.summary: Use a dedicated AI project (not a single chat) to hold your business brief and research files so long ecommerce SEO workflows don't lose context.
cards.use_when: Starting any multi-step keyword, content or AI-visibility project for a store and you plan to paste many research files over several sessions.

cards.title: Understand GEO and the two new AI-visibility KPIs
cards.summary: Generative Engine Optimization is the practice of getting your brand into AI-generated answers, measured by citations and brand mentions rather than clicks alone.
cards.use_when: Deciding what success looks like for a store's presence in ChatGPT, AI overviews or Perplexity, and choosing metrics to track alongside organic traffic.

cards.title: Discard three common GEO myths before planning store content
cards.summary: Google penalizes thin content not AI-written content, the AI model you use is not a ranking factor, and traditional SEO still underpins AI visibility.
cards.use_when: When a stakeholder or agency argues for or against using AI to produce store product and category content.

cards.title: Translate customer language into keyword research, not expert terminology
cards.summary: Research the words buyers actually type, which often differ from industry jargon, and split the task into transactional and informational keywords.
cards.use_when: Choosing which search terms a product, category or landing page should target before writing copy or building pages.

cards.title: Run transactional keyword research and cluster it by page
cards.summary: Take each core commercial term through an SEO tool's overview and suggestions, save the related terms and cluster them so one page owns each topic.
cards.use_when: Building or restructuring category and product landing pages, and deciding which terms each commercial page should target.

cards.title: Mine People-Also-Ask questions for buying-guide content
cards.summary: Pull PAA questions at depth around a core term and turn them into FAQ and guide content that answers real pre-purchase doubts.
cards.use_when: Planning buying guides, FAQ blocks and supporting content that feeds shoppers toward your commercial pages.

cards.title: Answer fan-out queries to win AI citations
cards.summary: Fan-out queries are the internal follow-up questions an AI asks itself when handling a broad prompt; answering them in your content raises citation chances.
cards.use_when: Writing guide, FAQ or PDP content aimed at being cited by ChatGPT, AI overviews or Perplexity for a broad category question.

cards.title: Do a four-part competitor analysis to plan your page architecture
cards.summary: Study competitors' ranking keywords, winning pages, sitemap structure and backlink profile to decide how much content and how many pages your store needs.
cards.use_when: Planning a category/blog structure for a new store or a new product line, or diagnosing why competitors outrank you.

cards.title: Map distinct product and collection intents to useful store pages
cards.summary: Splitting every offering onto its own page is the single most important structural decision for ranking commercial pages.
cards.use_when: Planning product and collection architecture for an ecommerce catalog.

cards.title: Apply the 2-second rule to commercial page first folds
cards.summary: Within two seconds of landing, a visitor must know what you offer, where you offer it, and what to do next.
cards.use_when: Writing or reviewing the above-the-fold area of a product, category, service or payment landing page.

cards.title: Run a commercial-page checklist: intent, one keyword, schema, design, specifics
cards.summary: Five checks determine whether a product or collection page will perform, starting with search-intent match and including structured data and evidence.
cards.use_when: Finalising a new category, product or collection page before publishing.

cards.title: Check descriptive page headings and relevant product structured data
cards.summary: Every page should carry exactly one H1 that states the offering, with H2–H4 for everything else, plus verified structured data.
cards.use_when: Auditing on-page technical setup across a store's templates, especially after theme changes or migrations.

cards.title: Write content capsules so AI engines can extract clean answers
cards.summary: Place a short, self-contained 20–25 word answer directly under each question heading so AI engines can lift it as a citation.
cards.use_when: Writing buying guides, blog posts and FAQ sections on product or category pages aimed at AI citations.

cards.title: Prompt an AI to draft capsule-style content from your keyword research
cards.summary: Feed the AI your brief, topic, audience and selected keywords to produce a structured capsule-format draft with sources and first-hand experience slots.
cards.use_when: Drafting buying guides, comparison posts or FAQ-driven blog content that should be extractable by AI engines.

cards.title: Build a content map that routes keywords to the right page type
cards.summary: Use your cluster data to assign each keyword to a commercial page, FAQ, or full article, so supporting content feeds the money pages.
cards.use_when: Planning an editorial calendar or deciding whether a keyword deserves its own page, a section, or an FAQ entry.

cards.title: Use citations and first-hand experience as AI-trust signals
cards.summary: Backing claims with sources and adding lived experience to your content increases trust with readers and citation likelihood with AI engines.
cards.use_when: Writing or reviewing any buying guide, comparison page or product explanation where factual claims and prices are stated.

cards.title: Iterate to a proven page template before scaling across the catalog
cards.summary: Perfect one commercial page against the checklist, then replicate the structure across other offerings and page types.
cards.use_when: Scaling a store's page production after the first category or service page performs structurally well.

cards.title: Draft and edit long-form content in an editable AI canvas
cards.summary: Use an AI assistant that renders the draft in an editable document so you can refine sections, then paste cleanly into your CMS.
cards.use_when: Producing a long-form blog post or category guide for your store and you want an iterative editing loop rather than copy-pasting from chat.

cards.title: Limit AI-generated question lists to keep content focused
cards.summary: If the model proposes too many sub-questions, cap them so the page stays tight and useful rather than bloated.
cards.use_when: Generating FAQ or Q&A sections for a store guide or informational landing page and the model returns an excessive question list.

cards.title: Add illustrations to break up text-heavy content (with ecommerce application)
cards.summary: Turn key passages into simple illustrations using a free text-to-visual tool, then convert and place them for impact.
cards.use_when: A product-education section, buying guide, or PDP long-description block reads as a wall of text and you want to make a specific point pop.

cards.title: Write meta descriptions with an AI assist and length target
cards.summary: Have the AI draft the meta description at under ~150 characters to support click-through, then paste into your SEO plugin.
cards.use_when: Finishing a store blog post or category page and you need the title tag and meta description fields filled before publishing.

cards.title: Map the whole site structure before building the store
cards.summary: Generate a CSV-style page map (URL, name, title tag, page type, focus) from prior research so the site is planned, not improvised.
cards.use_when: Planning a new store build or a major site restructure and you want the URL hierarchy and page list defined before writing pages.

cards.title: Deploy the new store and submit it to search consoles
cards.summary: Connect Google Search Console and submit your sitemap so the launched site can actually be found and indexed.
cards.use_when: Just after launching or relaunching an ecommerce site, when you need it discoverable in organic and AI search.

cards.title: Audit on-page SEO across five core elements plus speed
cards.summary: Check title tag, meta description, H1, H2s, and schema — plus page speed — using a free browser plugin and Lighthouse.
cards.use_when: Reviewing your own newly launched store or a site you're optimizing, and you want a fast on-page pass without deep technical work.

cards.title: Build purposeful internal links into every content page
cards.summary: Internal links improve crawlability, navigation, and pass authority — so link blog content to service/money pages where it makes sense.
cards.use_when: Publishing evergreen store content (buying guides, how-tos, blog posts) and you want it to feed your commercial pages.

cards.title: Track AI visibility with Search Console and Bing AI performance
cards.summary: Use clicks, impressions, average position, and queries from Search Console, and Bing's AI performance tab for citations.
cards.use_when: Monitoring whether your store is surfacing in AI overviews and chat results, and deciding what to do next month.

cards.title: Track brand mentions and cited queries, not just rankings
cards.summary: Mentions across Google AI overviews, ChatGPT, and Perplexity are tracked as a leading indicator alongside clicks.
cards.use_when: Deciding which AI-visibility signals to watch for your store and whether your brand is being recommended.

cards.title: Start with free local citations before any backlink strategy
cards.summary: Build local directory listings with consistent NAP as the first, cheapest authority layer for a local store.
cards.use_when: Launching a local store and you need foundational authority before investing in link campaigns.

cards.title: Earn expert citations through reporter-request platforms
cards.summary: Answer journalist/publisher questions on a connectivity platform to earn citations and brand mentions with a backlink.
cards.use_when: You or your store's founder have subject-matter authority and want authentic links without buying them.

cards.title: Evaluate sponsored placements by buyer relevance and referral value
cards.summary: If you still can't outrank competitors, buy relevant, high-quality links from vetted agencies — never quantity-focused cheap links.
cards.use_when: After you've built the site correctly, published good content, and gotten indexed — and you still aren't outranking competitors.

cards.title: AEO mental model: execute like Google, measure like Facebook
cards.summary: Treat answer-engine optimization as SEO-style content work but measure it with ad-style attribution (view-through, self-reported) rather than click-through, because AI referrals are invisible to analytics.
cards.use_when: Deciding how to resource and measure an AEO/generative-search channel for your store, when direct referrer traffic looks flat or falling but you suspect AI assistants are driving discovery.

cards.title: Platform-by-platform AEO playbooks diverge: don't run one strategy
cards.summary: Reddit's influence is largely isolated to ChatGPT, and the playbooks for ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Gemini and Google AI Overviews differ substantially.
cards.use_when: Allocating limited content and community effort across AI surfaces that send or influence traffic to your store (e.g., deciding whether a Reddit push will help Perplexity visibility).

cards.title: Prioritize AI discovery surfaces using the store's own buyer evidence
cards.summary: Consumer/prosumer discovery concentrates heavily in ChatGPT, while enterprise-tool research happens in Claude and Copilot, so platform priority should flip by segment.
cards.use_when: Allocating an ecommerce AI-discovery budget across assistants serving retail or wholesale buyers.

cards.title: Reddit playbook: open-ecosystem wedge posts and competitor-comparison framing
cards.summary: Succeed on Reddit by posting value-oriented content that leverages your tool's interoperability and explicit competitor comparisons, and avoid brand-only self-promotion.
cards.use_when: Planning Reddit participation to earn ChatGPT citations and reach buyers in relevant subreddits without posts being removed.

cards.title: Measure citation pickup and persistence before timing a store campaign
cards.summary: New Reddit content takes roughly 30-45 days to be cited by ChatGPT but can be cited by Perplexity as fast as the next day, informing how early to seed content.
cards.use_when: Timing Reddit or community content pushes ahead of a product launch or seasonal campaign when you need citations live by a specific date.

cards.title: Test question-led product content while preserving shopper usefulness
cards.summary: For AEO-designated initiatives, allocate roughly 80% of effort to agent/crawler consumption and 20% to human readability so content still makes sense if a human finds it.
cards.use_when: Producing YouTube videos, LinkedIn content, or blog posts with the explicit intent of earning AI citations rather than direct human clicks.

cards.title: Compete in AI citation by niching down the prompt, then expanding
cards.summary: You cannot win broad AI queries like 'best CRM', so start with narrow, defensible prompt phrasings, build topical authority, then attempt broader terms.
cards.use_when: Targeting AI-assistant answers in a crowded product category where broad 'best X' queries are dominated by incumbents.

cards.title: AEO channel priority and citation-lifetime tracking
cards.summary: Own-site content is cited fastest and most controllably; track citation share manually to detect when citations expire.
cards.use_when: Deciding where to publish before your own site versus third-party channels, and setting up a lightweight system to monitor AI citation retention.

cards.title: Test additional publishing surfaces against observed category citations
cards.summary: When Reddit is saturated, extend AEO content into Medium, Quora, and Substack, which are cited but less contested.
cards.use_when: Scaling AEO reach after you've established a Reddit and own-site presence and need additional citable surfaces.

cards.title: Understand retrieval vs memorization to choose content tactics
cards.summary: LLMs either retrieve fresh web content (~60% of ChatGPT queries per the source) or answer from trained-in knowledge (~40%), and each mode needs different AEO tactics.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to invest in fresh web content or in seeding training-data surfaces, given that the two modes respond to different inputs.

cards.title: Audit search crawler access independently from training permissions
cards.summary: Verify public product and collection pages are accessible to the intended search crawlers while preserving separate training choices.
cards.use_when: A store wants product pages discoverable in AI search or is diagnosing missing product visibility after CDN or theme changes.

cards.title: Submit sitemaps and confirm indexation as an AI visibility prerequisite
cards.summary: AI engines pull fresh information from Google and Bing, so an unindexed store will not be recommended in AI answers.
cards.use_when: Setting up an ecommerce store for AI visibility, or diagnosing why AI engines describe your brand inaccurately or not at all.

cards.title: Publish an About/Facts page as structured brand context for AI
cards.summary: A facts page giving what you do, your USPs and how long you've operated gives AI engines the raw material to describe and recommend you correctly.
cards.use_when: Building or refreshing the homepage/about section of an ecommerce store so AI engines can state accurate brand facts in recommendations.

cards.title: Validate structured product and brand facts alongside visible copy
cards.summary: Structured data spells out your business, products and social profiles in a machine-readable format AI crawlers read reliably.
cards.use_when: Adding or auditing structured data on an ecommerce site to improve how LLMs interpret brand and product information.

cards.title: Front-load answers on product and category pages with a TL;DR
cards.summary: Put a direct 2-4 sentence answer and a TL;DR at the top of every important page because most AI citations come from the first third of the page.
cards.use_when: Writing or rewriting product pages, category pages, buying guides and landing pages so AI extracts your content as the cited answer.

cards.title: Build FAQ sections from 'People Also Ask' to grow topical authority
cards.summary: Harvest the questions Google surfaces for your topic and answer them at the bottom of every important page to demonstrate expertise to AI.
cards.use_when: Adding Q&A coverage to product pages, category pages or buying guides to increase the chance AI engines treat your store as the expert source.

cards.title: Use comparison tables and head-to-head competitor pages to win AI recommendations
cards.summary: Head-to-head comparison pages and tables give AI engines an easy, digestible reason to recommend you over larger competitors it already knows.
cards.use_when: Competing against bigger, better-known brands in your category in AI search, or structuring comparison content on an ecommerce site.

cards.title: Replace vague claims with hard numbers, expert quotes and original data
cards.summary: High-quality content with specific figures, named expert quotes and at least one piece of original data is more likely to be cited by AI engines.
cards.use_when: Improving the citability of product pages, buying guides, blog posts and category content that currently relies on generic marketing language.

cards.title: Refresh evergreen content and surface a clear last-updated date
cards.summary: Stale content loses to fresh competitors in AI answers, so revisit key pages every couple of months and show the last-updated date.
cards.use_when: Maintaining a content library or buying-guide set on an ecommerce site that has not been refreshed recently and is losing AI citations.

cards.title: Fix NAP consistency and directory listings to stop AI misdescribing your store
cards.summary: Inconsistent name, address, phone and inconsistent descriptions across directories cause AI engines to produce wrong information about your business.
cards.use_when: Cleaning up brand presence for a store with physical locations, local service areas or notable B2B distribution, so AI shops describe it accurately.

cards.title: Get into 'best of' listicles and roundup articles that AI cites
cards.summary: AI engines frequently draw recommendations from '10 best X' listicles, so securing placement there directly increases the chance your store gets recommended.
cards.use_when: Acquiring recommendations in AI answers for a category where buyer queries surface best-of roundups (e.g. 'best [category] for [use case]').

cards.title: Use AI-generated buying criteria as hypotheses for a product-content audit
cards.summary: Prompt AI engines for the criteria they use to recommend your category, then retrofit your website and directory descriptions to match those criteria.
cards.use_when: Setting the target for what your store's descriptions, PDPs and directory listings should contain in order to be recommended in AI answers.

cards.title: Run an AI brand audit to find and correct the sources AI reads about you
cards.summary: Asking AI to search the internet and report what it knows about your brand reveals the exact sources shaping its view so you can fix them.
cards.use_when: Diagnosing why AI engines describe an ecommerce store incorrectly, omit key categories, or recommend competitors instead.

cards.title: Earn third-party mentions, podcasts and video to build AI trust
cards.summary: AI has no personal experience, so it looks for consensus; mentions in trusted publications, podcasts and video transcripts supply that consensus for your brand.
cards.use_when: Building authority signals for an ecommerce brand in a competitive category where reviews and editorial coverage influence AI recommendations.

cards.title: Collect honest product-experience reviews on relevant platforms
cards.summary: Because AI has no first-hand experience, it leans on customer reviews — especially ones that state concrete results — to decide whether to recommend you.
cards.use_when: Designing post-purchase review requests for ecommerce buyers and deciding which review destinations matter for product research.

cards.title: Engage Reddit communities with F5Bot monitoring to earn long-term AI citations
cards.summary: Reddit is one of the most-cited sources in AI answers, and cited posts are typically over a year old, so consistent value-first participation compounds.
cards.use_when: Building durable category presence and word-of-mouth for a store where buyers discuss products in Reddit threads and forums.

cards.title: Publish long-form LinkedIn articles structured for AI extraction
cards.summary: Long-form LinkedIn articles get indexed by Google and can therefore become AI-cited sources, unlike short posts.
cards.use_when: Extending an ecommerce brand's content footprint onto LinkedIn to create additional citable sources about your products and expertise.

cards.title: Use YouTube and video transcripts as a brand and AI citation channel
cards.summary: Video transcripts are indexed and cited by AI engines, so publishing videos about your products adds a durable discoverable source.
cards.use_when: Planning a video/content channel extension for an ecommerce brand to increase AI and Google discoverability.

cards.title: Publish transparent original product research through relevant press channels
cards.summary: Framing a listicle as a data-backed industry report and distributing it via a press wire is presented as one of the highest-ROI AI visibility moves.
cards.use_when: A category-level push to become the cited authority in AI answers, especially for a store or brand with data it can package as research.

cards.title: Execute a one-week AI visibility quick-win sequence
cards.summary: A prioritized starter list of free and low-cost actions to materially improve AI visibility within a week.
cards.use_when: An ecommerce operator starting AI visibility work and needing an ordered, immediately actionable checklist.

cards.title: Build Share of Voice, Not Rank #1
cards.summary: In answer engines the LLM summarizes many citations, so being cited most often beats being the top URL.
cards.use_when: Deciding what to optimize on a PDP, category page or landing page when you want your brand named in ChatGPT or Gemini answers for 'best X' queries.

cards.title: On-Site vs Off-Site AEO: Two Workstreams
cards.summary: Split answer-engine work into on-site pages (SEO plus long-tail product Q&A) and off-site citation groups (video, UGC, affiliates, blogs).
cards.use_when: Planning headcount or agency scope for an ecommerce brand's AEO program.

cards.title: Do AEO Early Even When You Skip SEO
cards.summary: Unlike SEO, answer engines can surface a new brand within days of a citation, so early-stage and low-authority stores should prioritize AEO and skip domain-authority-dependent SEO.
cards.use_when: Deciding where to spend content budget for a new or low-authority ecommerce brand.

cards.title: The Long Tail Is Bigger in Chat Than in Search
cards.summary: Average chat queries run ~25 words versus ~6 for search, and include follow-ups never searched before — a large, winnable long-tail of specific product questions.
cards.use_when: Choosing which product-detail and FAQ content to write for PDPs, help centers and landing pages.
